neighbours.label: the word just before a vague amount or extra quantity follows (may require | more, give you | multiple, much | farther)
fire: Large rooms with high ceilings may require more than one heater in winter.
Upgrading to the premium plan will give you multiple accounts for the family.
With a good pair of binoculars you can see much farther across the valley.
If the soil is very dry, increase the watering to twice a day.
Older dogs often need more rest than puppies after a long walk.
A thicker rope will let you lift much heavier loads safely.
Some stubborn stains may require several washes before they disappear.
Joining the club early will earn you extra points on every purchase.
quiet: Large rooms with high ceilings feel cold in winter without a heater.
Upgrading to the premium plan costs nine dollars for the family.
With a good pair of binoculars you can watch birds across the valley.
If the soil is very dry, water the plants in the early morning.
Older dogs often sleep near the door after a long walk.
A thicker rope is easier to grip when you lift loads.
Some stubborn stains come out with cold water and soap.
Joining the club early is free for students and teachers.

notes: Top examples peak on ' much', ' require', ' you', ' increase' right before 'more/multiple/farther/that area to 150'. Output promotes low/enough/multiple/separate and suppresses number words; the - pole fires on 'For example,' before a worked numeric case. Probe was weak (0.02-0.14), so low confidence.
